arXiv:2301.07708v1 [math.AP] 18 Jan 2023

Global Existence of solutions for systems of coupled reaction diffusion equations with nonlinearities of unlimited growth.

Said Kouachi Affiliation: Abbes Laghrour University, Khenchela, Algeria.
Abstract

In this work we prove global existence and uniform boundedness of solutions of 2×\times2 reaction-diffusion systems with control of mass structure and nonlinearities of unlimited growth. Furthermore the results are obtained without restrictions on diffusion terms neither on the initial data. Such systems possess many applications in physical-chemistry. Our technique of proof relies on a judiciously rectified Lyapunov functional used previously by the author in several papers

1 Introduction

In this article, we are concerned with the existence of globally bounded solutions to the reaction-diffusion system

{∂u∂t−a​Δ​u=f⁡(u,v),∂v∂t−b​Δ​v=g⁡(u,v),inℝ+×Ω,\left\{\begin{array}[]{c}\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}-a\Delta u=f(u,v),\\ \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial t}-b\Delta v=g(u,v),\\ \end{array}\right.\quad\mathrm{in}\quad\mathbb{R}^{+}\times\Omega, (1)

subject to the boundary conditions

∂u∂η=∂v∂η=0o​nℝ+×∂Ω\frac{\partial u}{\partial\eta}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial\eta}=0\qquad on\quad\mathbb{R}^{+}\times\partial\Omega (2)

and the initial data

u(0,x)=u0(x),v(0,x)=v0(x)inΩu(0,x)=u_{0}(x),\qquad v(0,x)=v_{0}(x)\qquad\mathrm{in}\quad\Omega (3)

where a>0a>0 and b>0b>0 are the diffusion coefficients of some interacting species whose spatiotemporal densities are uu and vv. The domain Ω\Omega is an open bounded domain of class C1C^{1} in ℝn\mathbb{R}^{n}, with boundary ∂Ω\partial\Omega and ∂∂η\frac{\partial}{\partial\eta} denotes the outward derivative on ∂Ω\partial\Omega. The initial data are assumed to be nonnegative and bounded. The reactions ff and gg are continuously differentiable functions. We suppose that, for some positive constants CC and μ\mu we have

f(u,v)≤f(u,v)+μg(u,v)≤0, for all u≥0,v≥0 with u+v≥C.f(u,v)\leq f(u,v)+\mu g(u,v)\leq 0,\text{ for all }u\geq 0,\ v\geq 0\text{ with }u+v\geq C. (4)

The last inequality is called ”the control of mass condition”.
We suppose f⁡(0,v)=0f(0,v)=0 and g⁡(u,0)≥0,g(u,0)\geq 0, for all u≥0u\geq 0 andv≥0\ v\geq 0, then using standard comparison arguments for parabolic equations (see e.g. [5]) the solutions remain positive at any time.

In the case of systems on the form

{∂u∂t−a​Δ​u=−u​F​(v),∂v∂t−b​Δ​v=u​G​(v),inℝ+×Ω,\left\{\begin{array}[]{c}\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}-a\Delta u=-uF(v),\\ \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial t}-b\Delta v=uG(v),\\ \end{array}\right.\quad\mathrm{in}\quad\mathbb{R}^{+}\times\Omega, (5)

[4] generalized the results of K. Masuda for F⁡(v)=G⁡(v)=vβF(v)=G(v)=v^{\beta} to nonlinearities F⁡(s)F(s) satisfying the condition

lims→+∞[ln⁡(1+F⁡(s))s]=0,\displaystyle\lim_{s\rightarrow+\infty}\left[\frac{\ln\left(1+F(s)\right)}{s}\right]=0, (6)

which extends the nonlinearities to sub-linear ones (e.g. F(v)=G(v)=evγ, 0<γ<1)F(v)=G(v)=e^{v^{\gamma}},\;0<\gamma<1). In the case of nonlinearities of exponential growth like F⁡(v)=G⁡(v)=evF(v)=G(v)=e^{v} which appears in the Frank-Kamenetskii approximation to Arrhenius-type reaction [2], [3] has made a small progress in this direction and proved that solutions are globally bounded under the condition ‖u0‖∞≤8​a​b/(a−b)2||u_{0}||_{\infty}\leq 8ab/(a-b)^{2}. Then [17] proved (in the case 0<b<a<∞0<b<a<\infty which means that the absorbed substance diffuses faster than the other one) that global solutions exist if Ω=ℝn\Omega=\mathbb{R}^{n}. The proof is based on a simple comparison property concerning the kernels associated with the operators (∂∂t−a​Δ)\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial t}-a\Delta\right) and (∂∂t−b​Δ).\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial t}-b\Delta\right). Some years ago, [6] obtained similar results (in the general case). Then the authors in [16] generalized the results obtained in [4] while adding −c​Δ​u-c\Delta u to the right-hand side of the second equation of system (1) under the condition

l​i​ms→+∞​[l​o​g​(1+f⁡(r,s))s]<α∗​, for any​r≥0,\underset{s\rightarrow+\infty}{lim}\left[\frac{log\left(1+f(r,s)\right)}{s}\right]<\alpha^{\ast}\text{, for\ any}\;r\geq 0,

where f⁡(r,s)≥0f(r,s)\geq 0 for all r,s≥0r,\ s\geq 0 and

α∗=2​a​bn​(a−b)2​‖u0‖∞,\alpha^{\ast}=\frac{2ab}{n(a-b)^{2}\left\|u_{0}\right\|_{\infty}},

condition reflecting the weak exponential growth of the reaction term ff. [8] and then [7] proved global existence of solutions of (5) on bounded domains if a>ba>b or c≥a−b>0c\geq a-b>0, while in [9] it is showed that solutions exist globally whenever b>a,c<b−ab>a,\ c<b-a and G⁡(v)G(v) is of exponential growth. Recently in [13] we proved global existence of solutions of (5) in a bounded domain under the condition

limv→+∞G′​(v)F⁡(v)=0,\displaystyle\lim_{v\rightarrow+\infty}\frac{G^{\prime}(v)}{F(v)}=0, (7)

where G′G^{\prime} denotes the first derivative of GG with respect to vv and the functions FF, GG, G′G^{\prime} and G′′G^{\prime\prime}are continuously differentiable and nonnegative.
To the best of our knowledge, the question of global existence of reaction diffusion systems on a bounded domain remains open when the reactions grow faster than a polynomial. Some partial positive results have been obtained only when the reactions grow faster than a polynomial as it is cited above (see [13] and [3] when Ω\Omega is bounded and [17] in the unbounded case or when Ω=ℝn\Omega=\mathbb{R}^{n}). We should know that, in some cases, solutions of system (1) with appropriate boundary conditions can plow-up in finite time (see for example [21, 22]).

In this paper we show the global existence of a unique solution (uniformly bounded on ℝ+×Ω\mathbb{R}^{+}\times\Omega) to problem (1)-(3) without conditions on the nonlinearities growth (i.e. condition (4)) as it was supposed until now. Remark that for system (5), conditions like (7) are more stronger then (4) when the reactions grow faster than a polynomial, especially when F=G.F=G.

2 Statement of the main results

It is well known that, for any initial data in L∞​(Ω)L^{\infty}(\Omega), local existence and uniqueness of classical solutions to the initial value problem (1)-(3) follows from the basic existence theory for abstract semi-linear differential equations (see [1], [5] or [22]). The solutions are classical on (0,Tmax),(0,T_{\max}), where TmaxT_{\max} denotes the eventual blowing-up time in L∞​(Ω)L^{\infty}(\Omega). If we denote by

‖u‖∞=maxx∈Ω⁡|u⁡(x)|,\left\|u\right\|_{\infty}\;=\;\max_{x\in\Omega}\left|u(x)\right|,

the usual norm in the space L∞​(Ω)L^{\infty}(\Omega)\ (or C⁡(Ω¯)C\left(\overline{\Omega}\right)), let us recall the following classical local existence result under the above assumptions:

Proposition 1

The problem(1)-(3) admits a unique, classical solution (u,v)(u,v) on (0,Tmax[×Ω(0,T_{\max}[\times\Omega. If Tmax<∞T_{\max}<\infty then

limt↗Tmax{‖u(t,.)‖∞+‖v(t,.)‖∞}=∞.\lim_{t\nearrow T_{\max}}\left\{\left\|u(t,.)\right\|_{\infty}+\left\|v(t,.)\right\|_{\infty}\right\}=\infty.

Then we can formulate our main result as follows:

Theorem 2

Under condition (4), the solution of problem (1)-(3) with positive initial data in 𝕃∞​(Ω)\mathbb{L}^{\infty}(\Omega) exists globally in time. Moreover uu and vv are uniformly bounded with

‖u(t,.)‖∞≤u¯0 and ‖v(t,.)‖∞≤v¯0, for all t>0,\left\|u(t,.)\right\|_{\infty}\leq\overline{u}_{0}\text{ and \ }\left\|v(t,.)\right\|_{\infty}\leq\overline{v}_{0},\text{ for all }t>0, (8)

where

u¯0=sup{C,‖u0‖∞}​ and ​v¯0=sup{C,‖v0‖∞},\overline{u}_{0}=\sup\left\{C,\left\|u_{0}\right\|_{\infty}\right\}\text{ and }\overline{v}_{0}=\sup\left\{C,\left\|v_{0}\right\|_{\infty}\right\}, (9)

and CC given by (4).

For example our results are applicable to system (5) for F⁡(v)=eev−P⁡(v)F(v)=e^{e^{v}}-P(v) and G⁡(v)=eev,G(v)=e^{e^{v}}, where PP is any polynomial (even zero polynomial) of finite degree.

This result can be formulated by the following

Corollary 3

The solutions of system (5) with boundary conditions (2) and positive initial data in 𝕃∞​(Ω)\mathbb{L}^{\infty}(\Omega) are global and uniformly bounded on [0,+∞[×Ω\left[0,+\infty\right[\times\Omega with

‖u(t,.)‖∞≤‖u0‖∞ and ‖v(t,.)‖∞≤v¯0, for all t>0,\left\|u(t,.)\right\|_{\infty}\leq\left\|u_{0}\right\|_{\infty}\text{ and \ }\left\|v(t,.)\right\|_{\infty}\leq\overline{v}_{0},\text{ for all }t>0,

provided that

0<lims→+∞F⁡(s)G⁡(s)≤+∞.0<\lim_{s\rightarrow+\infty}\frac{F(s)}{G(s)}\leq+\infty.

Another application of Theorem 2, is the following system modelling the exothermic combustion in a gas

{∂Y∂t−a​Δ​Y=−Ym​eT,∂T∂t−b​Δ​T=Ym​eT,inℝ+×Ω,\left\{\begin{array}[]{ccc}\frac{\partial Y}{\partial t}-a\Delta Y&=&-Y^{m}e^{T},\\ \frac{\partial T}{\partial t}-b\Delta T&=&Y^{m}e^{T},\end{array}\right.\quad\mathrm{in}\quad\mathbb{R}^{+}\times\Omega, (10)

where YY is the concentration of a single reactant, TT is the temperature (see e.g. [20] in the case when the function eTe^{T} is approximated by a polynomial and [6] in more general case). Moreover, we have the following result

Corollary 4

The system (10) with boundary conditions (2) and positive initial data in 𝕃∞​(Ω)\mathbb{L}^{\infty}(\Omega) has global and uniformly bounded solutions on [0,+∞[×Ω\left[0,+\infty\right[\times\Omega satisfying

‖Y(t,.)‖∞≤‖Y(0,.)‖∞ and ‖T(t,.)‖∞≤‖T(0,.)‖∞, for all t≥0.\left\|Y(t,.)\right\|_{\infty}\leq\left\|Y(0,.)\right\|_{\infty}\text{ and \ }\left\|T(t,.)\right\|_{\infty}\leq\left\|T(0,.)\right\|_{\infty},\text{ for all }t\geq 0.

θi​θi+2θi+12=θ2,i=0,1,…,p.\dfrac{\theta_{i}\theta_{i+2}}{\theta_{i+1}^{2}}=\theta^{2},\ \ \ \ i=0,1,...,p. (12)

Then condition (12) gives the positivity of the quadratics Ti​(∇u,∇v)T_{i}\left(\nabla u,\nabla v\right) to get I≤0I\leq 0 on (0,Tmax)\left(0,T_{\max}\right).

lims→+∞F⁡(s)G⁡(s)>λ,\lim_{s\rightarrow+\infty}\frac{F(s)}{G(s)}>\lambda,

F⁡(s)G⁡(s)>λ, for all ​s>A.\frac{F(s)}{G(s)}>\lambda,\text{ for all }s>A.

Remark 5

Theorem 2 is applicable for more general boundary conditions than (2) as homogenous and nonhomogenous Dirichlet and mixed boundary conditions.

Remark 6

Condition (4) should be taken with prudence: It can arrive that it is not satisfied for systems with simple reaction of polynomial growth. It is the case, for example when f⁡(u,v)=(u−u2)​v2f(u,v)=\left(u-u^{2}\right)v^{2} and g⁡(u,v)=u​v2g(u,v)=uv^{2} where the solution blows up at finite time for initial data 12≤u0≤1\frac{1}{2}\leq u_{0}\leq 1 on Ω.\Omega. Indeed the region

∑={(u,v)∈ℝ+2 such that 12≤u≤1},\sum=\left\{\left(u,v\right)\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{2}\text{ such that }\frac{1}{2}\leq u\leq 1\right\},

is an inariant region which gives g⁡(u,v)≥12​v2g(u,v)\geq\frac{1}{2}v^{2} in ∑\sum, then by comparison arguments we get blow up at finite time. Obviously we can not find positive constants CC and λ\lambda such that (4) is satisfied.

Conclusion 7

The global existence of solutions to systems of a coupled reaction diffusion equations with unlimited nonlineraties growth had been open until very recently except for some partial results under very restrictive conditions as small initial data. The main reason to obtain interesting results in such situation is the lack of the classical methods as those based on the entropy inequality or those using the duality argument etc… In this work we used a very simple functional but very strong solving the problem of global existence of reaction diffusion systems without conditions on the nonlineraties growth.
